segments.text: The metallic colossus, the historicist blueprint of history and the sovereign triumph of Christ.
From the impasse of human wisdom to the stone that fills the earth,
God's unbroken chain of empires and Christ's everlasting kingdom.
Big idea.
Nebuchadnezzar's forgotten dream is God's legal decree and historical roadmap.
All human dominion is bounded, transient, and destined to be replaced by the everlasting kingdom of Jesus Christ.
From The Last Sitting, sheet 1.
In chapter 1, Daniel and his companions proved that covenant faithfulness at the table
preceded the gift of wisdom.
Now in chapter 2, that wisdom is tested on the global stage
when the emperor dreams of the fate of all human empires.
And heaven, not Babylon's magicians, defines what shall be in the latter days.
The impasse of human wisdom.
Daniel 2, verses 1 through 28.
Babylon, c. 603 BC.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's sole reign, around 603 BC,
the king of Babylon was awakened by a terrifying nightmare that left his spirit deeply agitated.
Daniel 2, verses 1.
Seeking certainty, the king summoned his occult counselors, the magicians,
enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans, and placed before them an impossible demand.
Tell him the dream he had forgotten, along with its interpretation, or face immediate execution.
Daniel 2, verses 5 through 8.
Babylon's intellectual elite confessed their utter bankruptcy.
There is not a man upon the earth that can chew the king's matter,
except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.
Daniel 2, verses 10 through 11.
When the royal execution decree went forth, Daniel and his companions did not panic.
They held an emergency prayer session,
petitioning the god of heaven for mercy concerning the secret.
Daniel 2, verses 17 through 18.
In a night vision, God revealed both the dream and its meaning.
Standing before the emperor, Daniel deflected all praise from human intellect to divine sovereignty.
There is a god in heaven that revealeth secrets,
and maketh known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days.
Daniel 2, 28.
The forgotten dream was not an ancient puzzle designed to satisfy curiosity.
It was God's legal decree and historical roadmap, establishing that all human dominion
is strictly bounded, transient, and destined to be replaced by the everlasting kingdom of Jesus Christ.
Text 1.
Human wisdom failed.
Daniel prayed.
God revealed secrets.
The dream governs the latter days.
The king's magicians do not.
Main point 1.
The historicist chain of world empires.
Daniel 2, 31 to 40.
Nebuchadnezzar saw an immense, dazzling statue standing before him.
Its anatomy was composed of five distinct sections,
a head of fine gold, a chest and arms of silver,
a belly and thighs of bronze, legs of iron,
and feet made of iron mixed with ceramic clay.
Daniel 2, 32, 33.
This sequence presents an unbroken, continuous chain of empires in historical time.
Head of gold, Babylon, 605 to 539 BC.
Daniel identifies the starting point without ambiguity.
Thou art this head of gold, Daniel 38.
Scripture calls Babylon the golden city, Isaiah 14, 4.
Chest and arms of silver, Medo-Persia, 539 to 331 BC.
Daniel announces that after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee.
Daniel 2, 39.
Babylon fell to the dual Medo-Persian empire under Cyrus the Great in 539 BC.
Daniel 5, 30, 31.
Scripture later explicitly identifies Medo-Persia as Babylon's successor, Daniel 8, 20.
Belly and thighs of bronze, Greece, 331 to 168 BC.
A third kingdom of brass which shall bear rule over all the earth followed.
Alexander the Great dismantled the Persian empire at Arbela, Gagamela, in 331 BC,
clothing his armies in bronze armor and spreading Greek language and culture throughout the ancient
world. Scripture explicitly names Greece as the power that shatters Medo-Persia, Daniel 8, 21.
Legs of iron, Imperial Rome, 168 BC to AD 476.
The fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron.
For as much as iron breaketh in pieces and subdue with all things.
Daniel 2, 40.
Following the Battle of Padna in 168 BC, Rome emerged as the Mediterranean's supreme power,
crushing opposition with military discipline, administrative cohesion, and iron weaponry.
Rome ruled for six centuries as a unified pagan empire.
The physical and moral gradients of the Colossus.
The Colossus is characterized by a dual gradient.
Specific gravity and value decline.
Gold has a specific gravity of 19.3 times the weight of water, silver 10.5, bronze 8.9,
and iron 7.8.
Value and density decline steadily from head to feet,
reflecting a progressive loss of monarchical unity and moral majesty.
Hardness and crushing force increase.
While gold and silver are malleable and soft, iron possesses brutal crushing force.
Imperial Rome was far less culturally refined than Babylon or Greece,
but it possessed unrivaled military destructiveness.
Interpretation.
Only the head is named in Daniel 2, 38.
Each later medal follows after thee in succession,
confirmed when Daniel 8 names Medo-Persia in Greece.
You start at the named head and walk the chain.
You do not restart it in a modern century.
Main point two.
The divided kingdoms and the mirage of unity.
The statue does not feature a fifth medal.
The legs of iron transition directly into feet composed of iron mixed with miry clay.
Daniel 2, 41 to 43.
This signifies that the fourth world empire would not be conquered by a fifth global empire.
Instead, it would fragment from within.
When the Western Roman Empire fractured under Germanic incursions in AD 476,
it divided into separate kingdoms that became the foundation of modern Europe.
Iron and clay.
What scripture means?
Clay in scripture, clay consistently symbolizes God's covenant or religious people in the hands
of the divine potter, Isaiah 64, 8, Jeremiah 18, 6.
While iron represents secular, coercive, civil statecraft,
clay represents religious authority.
The church-state fusion.
Beginning with Emperor Constantine and solidifying in the medieval Holy Roman Empire,
civil power, iron, was fused with ecclesiastical authority, clay.
Civil swords enforced religious dogmas and religious decrees directed civil armies.
The prophetic sentence, Daniel predicted that these fragmented powers would attempt to
reunite through political alliances and royal intermarriages.
They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men,
but they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay.
Daniel 2, 43.
For 15 centuries, every conqueror who sought to forge a unified European super state,
including Charlemagne, Charles V, Louis XIV, Napoleon Bonaparte,
Kaiser Wilhelm II, and Adolf Hitler, struck this divine barrier and failed.
The prophecy declared in advance, they shall not hold together.
They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men,
but they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay.
Daniel 2, 43.
Main point three, the redemptive climax.
The supernatural stone.
The focal point of the vision is not the metallic colossus,
but its total destruction by a supernatural agent.
Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands,
which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay,
and break them to pieces.
And the stone that smote the image became a great mountain
and filled the whole earth.
Daniel 2, 34 through 35, KJV.
One, the divine identity of the stone.
The stone is Jesus Christ.
The phrase cut out without hands denotes divine origin without human agency,
pointing to Christ's miraculous incarnation through the virgin birth,
his divine resurrection, and his supernatural second coming.
Scripture repeatedly identifies Jesus as the stone.
The stone rejected by the builders that becomes the chief cornerstone,
Psalm 118, 22, and 1 Peter 2, 6 through 8.
The rock upon which the church is built, 1 Corinthians 10, 4, Matthew 16, 18.
The stone that shatters all opposition, Luke 20, 17 through 18.
Two, the timing and nature of the impact.
The location of the strike.
The stone strikes the statue exclusively on its feet of iron and clay, Daniel 2, 34.
It did not strike during the Babylonian, Persian, Greek, or unified pagan Roman legs.
Verse 44 establishes the timeline.
And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom which shall never be
destroyed.
Christ's catastrophic universal kingdom arrives during the modern era of divided European nations.
Abolition, not political reformation.
The stone does not merge with the statue, reform its politics,
or Christianize its laws through social evolution.
It strikes the image with cataclysmic force, pulverizing all human empires until they become
like dust on a summer threshing floor.
Swept away by the wind, Daniel 2, 35.
A universal eternal domain.
After obliterating the colossus, the stone expands into a great mountain that fills the entire
planet.
The kingdom of God has no geographical limits, no successor, and no end.
Revelation 11, 15.
The redemptive choice.
Repentance or ruin.
Jesus applied this very prophecy to himself during his earthly ministry.
Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken, but on whosoever it shall fall,
it will grind him to powder.
Luke 2018, KGV.
Here is the gospel offer embedded in the metallic colossus.
If you fall upon Christ today in repentance, your pride is broken, your sins are forgiven
through his blood, and you are saved.
If you resist him, the stone will fall upon you in final judgment, sweeping away all earthly
security.
The stone is not a policy program or a better emperor.
It is Jesus Christ, cut without hands, striking the feet, filling the earth.
Build on the living stone today.
Next lesson, sheet 3, Daniel 3, the plane of Dura.
Because Babylon was shown only the head of gold, Nebuchadnezzar's next move will be
to build an image made entirely of gold and force the empire to worship it, the prototype
of the final crisis.
